verdict_meaning: This verdict records that the NEW value could not be independently corroborated from the permitted evidence, and that the one wiki-text argument the evidence does support points at the higher (old) figure. It is NOT a confirmed regression. Treat as 'change not corroborated — produce the scenario input tuple and the intended mechanism, then re-run the oracle'.

the established model uses a fixed `0.8·max_stacks` constant (with a `hits/2` short-fight branch). Under the engine's own ordering convention (4 leading ability hits apply stacks before the auto stream) the exact Cesaro mean of the capped ramp `min(k, C)` over `h` hits is `C - C(C-1)/(2h)` for `h >= C`; the constant model equals the exact mean at ~10 autos and deviates by up to +/-20% at the extremes.

independent_computation.step_0_target_quantity: applied_amount of a single healing event. Per S7 the golden healing-event record is applied = raw * factor.

step_1_ratio.rounding_band: with both leaves rounded to 1 dp the true ratio lies in [210.95/271.45, 211.05/271.35] = [0.777123, 0.777778]

step_2_eliminate_the_healing_reduction_l.argument: S4 fixes the ONLY healing-reduction mechanism in the engine as a multiplicative 0.60 with strongest-wins (min) composition and no stacking. For one event, any change in its wound state must therefore multiply applied_amount by exactly 0.60 (wound gained) or 1/0.60 = 1.6667 (wound lost). Composition changes cannot help either: min() over a set whose only member value is 0.60 can only ever yield 1.00 or 0.60.
step_2_eliminate_the_healing_reduction_l.conclusion: The healing-reduction factor did NOT change. The raw heal changed, by the same factor 0.7774503.

step_3_locate_the_raw_heal.argument: Per S3, neither item named in the scenario id heals or carries any healing-side stat (no lifesteal, no omnivamp, no heal-and-shield-power) and neither passive text (S1, S2) mentions healing. So the heal is champion-sourced. The only route by which a Black-Cleaver/Bloodsong scenario can move a champion heal by 22.255% is a damage-proportional heal (S8: Aatrox Umbral Dash = 16% of post-mitigation damage) fed by a 22.255% change in post-mitigation damage.

step_4_mitigation_identity.formula: S5: post = raw * 100/(100+R). With armor reduction fraction f applied to target armor A, post ∝ 1/(100 + (1-f)A). Dropping a reduction f therefore multiplies damage by (100 + (1-f)A)/(100+A), i.e. a drop of f*A/(100+A).

step_5_eliminations.hypothesis: H1 - Black Cleaver stack-model retune (S6): 0.8*max_stacks constant (= 0.8*5 = 4 stacks = 24% armor reduction, per S1's '6% per stack, 5 stacks, 30% max') replaced by the Cesaro mean C - C(C-1)/(2h) = 5 - 10/h stacks.
step_5_eliminations.max_possible_drop: even the extreme retune 24% -> 0% reduction yields only 0.24*A/(100+A); reaching 22.255% needs A = 1275 armor.
step_5_eliminations.verdict: RULED OUT. At the largest level-18 base armor in the cache (Sejuani, 126.65) the retune can move damage by at most 13.4%; at A = 200 by at most 16.0%.

step_5_eliminations.hypothesis: H2 - Bloodsong Expose Weakness amp alone (S2: 8% ranged-difference / 5%).

step_5_eliminations.verdict: POSSIBLE only against a heavily itemized tank; the largest level-18 BASE armor in data/champions.json is 126.65 (Sejuani), so this needs ~160 bonus armor on the target.

step_5_eliminations.hypothesis: H4 - Carve (30%) AND Expose Weakness both removed from this damage source.
step_5_eliminations.verdict: CONSISTENT at ordinary level-18 armor values.

step_6_scan_for_an_exact_fit.method: Computed level-18 base armor for all 173 cached champions via S10 (= flat + 17*perLevel, since (0.7025+0.0175*17) = 1.0 exactly) and tested H3/H4 for an exact ratio match inside the rounding band.
step_6_scan_for_an_exact_fit.result: One hit: Tryndamere, A = 115, H4 with the 8% value -> 0.777347 (inside band).
step_6_scan_for_an_exact_fit.significance: NOT evidence. d(ratio)/dA ~ -6.0e-4 per armor point, so the rounding band is ~1.1 armor units wide; across 173 candidate armors one hit is the chance expectation. Recorded and discarded.

step_7_what_the_wiki_text_says_about_the.argument: H3 and H4 both require the two items' effects to stop amplifying this participant's damage. Both effects are TARGET-side debuffs per the cached wiki text: Carve 'inflicts 6% armor reduction' on the enemy (armor is the target's own stat, so every attacker reads the reduced value), and Expose Weakness explicitly 'caus[es] them to take 8%:5% increased damage FROM ALL SOURCES' (S1, S2). In a roster fight the wiki therefore grants the amplification to every source, not just the wielder - which is the higher (old) figure.
step_7_what_the_wiki_text_says_about_the.counter_hypothesis_not_excluded: The same 22.255% drop is equally consistent with the old value having granted the debuffs to a participant that never legitimately had them - e.g. a wielder who deals no physical damage (Carve never stacks), a Spellblade that is not up at this event (S2: 4 s Expose Weakness duration, 1.5 s cooldown, requires an ability cast then a basic attack within 10 s), or a debuff mis-attributed across teams. Nothing in data/ or docs/math-foundations.md distinguishes these from the wiki-contradicting reading.

step_8_blocking_gap.statement: The leaf is NOT determinable from the permitted evidence. Reproducing an applied_amount requires the scenario's input tuple (participants and their teams, levels, ability ranks, per-participant item lists, fight mode and window, and which participant/event index 39 belongs to). That tuple is defined outside data/ and docs/math-foundations.md.

what_would_settle_it: The scenario input tuple for cleaver_bloodsong_roster (participants, teams, levels, ranks, per-participant items, fight mode/duration) and which participant healing_events[39] belongs to.

The sibling leaves of the same event: raw_amount, factor, source, time, trigger_source. If factor is unchanged (as step 2 proves it must be), raw_amount alone identifies whether the mechanism is Carve, Expose Weakness, both, or an unrelated damage-side change.

The target's total armor at the event time. H3 requires ~287; H4 requires ~115 (8%) or ~158 (5%). If the target's armor is ordinary and the drop is the full 22.255%, both item debuffs vanished from this source - which contradicts S1/S2's 'from all sources' / target-side-armor semantics unless the wielder legitimately never applied them.
conclusions_that_are_firm: The healing-reduction (Grievous Wounds) layer is NOT the cause: 0.7774503 is not reachable from the documented 0.60 strongest-wins factor (S4).
Neither Black Cleaver nor Bloodsong touches healing directly (S1, S2, S3); the moved quantity is a damage-proportional champion heal.

The Black Cleaver average-stacks retune recommended in docs/math-foundations.md Section 2.3 (S6) CANNOT by itself produce this diff - it would need 1275 target armor. If the change under test is that retune, the diff has a second, undisclosed cause.
Bloodsong's Expose Weakness amp alone cannot produce it either (max 7.41%).
